dimensions.rationale: POV no longer reproduces and the whole traversal class is closed, not just the observed payload — every mixed-separator and multi-level variant now returns null.
dimensions.evidence: pov_after_patch.log: 'normalize("//../secret.txt") rejected = true -> returned [null] ... SAFE'. Direct probe of the patched build: //../secret.txt, \\..\secret.txt, //..\secret.txt, \\../secret.txt, //./secret.txt, //../../secret.txt, ///../secret.txt, //..//secret.txt, //.././secret.txt, //a/../../secret.txt all -> normalize=[null]. The host part is by construction separator-free (indexOf from idx 2), so '.' and '..' are the only components with traversal semantics.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Fixes the flaw at the exact sink — the prefix computation that swallowed '..' — not a caller or symptom guard; identical location to the official fix.
dimensions.evidence: FilenameUtils.java:679-692 replaces 'return Math.min(posUnix, posWin) + 1;' in the isSeparator(ch0)&&isSeparator(ch1) UNC branch of getPrefixLength — the same statement upstream commit 2736b6fe0 replaces. Root flaw: doNormalize only rejects '..' after the prefix (i == prefix + 2 -> return null), so a '..' absorbed into the prefix was never evaluated.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: All traversal paths and separator variants covered via the single shared chokepoint; only the non-traversal invalid-hostname hardening from the official fix is missing.
dimensions.evidence: All normalize/normalizeNoEndSeparator overloads funnel through doNormalize -> getPrefixLength, so one fix covers every entry point (verified: normalizeNoEndSeparator("//../secret.txt") -> null). Both separator flavors handled (posUnix/posWin). Gap: getPrefixLength("\\\\-server\\a\\b\\c.txt") returns 10, official returns -1 — a malformed host name, not a directory escape.
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy at the identical location (validate the UNC host component, return NOT_FOUND), but a strictly weaker mechanism than the official allowlist.
dimensions.evidence: Ours: 'final String hostPart = filename.substring(2, pos); if (".".equals(hostPart) || "..".equals(hostPart)) return NOT_FOUND;'. Official 2736b6fe0: 'String hostnamePart = fileName.substring(2, pos - 1); return isValidHostName(hostnamePart) ? pos : NOT_FOUND;' — same extracted substring, same return contract, allowlist (isIPv4Address || isIPv6Address || isRFC3986HostName) instead of blocklist.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: No patch-attributable regressions: targeted suite fully green and all legitimate UNC forms preserved; the suite failures are pre-existing environmental noise proven on pristine code.
dimensions.evidence: regression_2.log: 'Tests run: 38, Failures: 0 - FilenameUtilsTestCase' + 'Tests run: 28, Failures: 0 - FileSystemUtilsTestCase', BUILD SUCCESS. Stashing the patch and re-running the 4 failures reproduces them identically on pristine code ('Tests run: 52, Failures: 4') — chmod/read-only assertions invalid under root; neither failing class references FilenameUtils. Legit paths intact: //server/a, //server/a/b/c.txt, //1.2.3.4/share/f, \\::1\a\b\c.txt, \\server.example.org\..., \\server.\... all unchanged.
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: No new weakness: substring bounds are provably safe, no regex introduced, no TOCTOU or crash surface.
dimensions.evidence: FilenameUtils.java:682 'filename.substring(2, pos)' — the pre-existing guard 'posUnix == 2 || posWin == 2' returns NOT_FOUND first, so pos >= 3, making substring(2, pos) always in-bounds (no StringIndexOutOfBounds). Pure string comparison, no Pattern/regex, so unlike the official fix it adds zero ReDoS surface. Probe of 21 inputs produced no exceptions.
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Tight, localized diff: one return statement in the correct method plus a focused regression test, no unrelated edits.
dimensions.evidence: patch_only.diff touches exactly one production hunk (FilenameUtils.java:679-692, ~10 lines) and one test method (FilenameUtilsTestCase.testNormalize_rejectsDoubleSeparatorDotDotPrefix). Compare: the official fix adds 147 lines to the same file.
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: Works and is exhaustive for traversal semantics, but uses a blocklist where the defense-of-record (and upstream) uses a host-name allowlist — the more fragile primitive.
dimensions.evidence: Ours enumerates the bad set: '".".equals(hostPart) || "..".equals(hostPart)'. Official validates the good set: isValidHostName = isIPv4Address || isIPv6Address || isRFC3986HostName (REG_NAME_PART_PATTERN '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$'). The canonicalize-then-verify-under-base anchor does not map here — this is a pure string-normalization API with no base dir — but the blocklist's under-rejection is demonstrable: '\\-server\a\b\c.txt' is accepted (official rejects).
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Strictly weaker than the official fix on host-name validation. Replaying the official upstream assertions (commit 2736b6fe0) against our patch yields 12/14 pass, 2 fail: normalize("\\\\-server\\a\\b\\c.txt") returns "//-server/a/b/c.txt" (official: null) and getPrefixLength("\\\\-server\\a\\b\\c.txt") returns 10 (official: -1). These are malformed-UNC hardening cases, not directory escapes, so they carry no traversal impact — but if the project later adopts the upstream test suite, these two assertions fail.

Blocklist mechanism ({".", ".."}) rather than the allowlist upstream chose. It is exhaustive here because the host part is separator-free by construction (indexOf from index 2), so only "." and ".." carry traversal semantics — but the primitive is inherently less future-proof than isValidHostName if the surrounding prefix-parsing logic ever changes.

The supplied taint trace points at FileSystemUtils.java (freeSpaceKb path -> Runtime.exec at line 573), which the patch does not touch. This appears to be finder mislocalization rather than a patch gap: CVE-2021-29425/IO-559 is FilenameUtils.normalize, the POV exercises normalize, and the official fix likewise touches only FilenameUtils.java.

Pipeline-level, not a patch defect: the run was auto-rejected with 'Regression command failed: mvn -B test', but all 4 failures (FileFilterTestCase.testCanRead/testCanWrite, FileUtilsCleanDirectoryTestCase.testThrowsOnNullList/testThrowsOnCannotDeleteFile) reproduce identically on pristine unpatched code because Maven runs as root and chmod-based read-only assertions do not hold for root. The rejection is a false positive and the verdict should be revisited.

result.root_cause: FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength blindly treated any text between a leading double separator and the next separator as a UNC host name and folded it into the immutable prefix, so a "." or ".." in that slot was never evaluated by doNormalize's parent-traversal check (which only rejects ".." occurring after the prefix via `i == prefix + 2 -> return null`), letting "//../foo" normalize to itself while the equivalent "/../foo" correctly returned null.
result.summary: This is a good, correctly-located fix that the pipeline rejected for the wrong reason. It replaces the exact same statement in getPrefixLength's UNC branch that the official upstream fix (commit 2736b6fe0, IO-559) replaces, extracting the identical host substring, and it closes the entire traversal class — every probed variant (mixed separators \\..\, //..\, \\../, multi-level //../../, ///../, //..//, //.././) now returns null, while legitimate UNC, IPv4, IPv6, and FQDN paths are preserved. The reported regression failure is a false positive: the same 4 tests (chmod/read-only assertions invalid under root in Docker) fail identically on pristine unpatched code and never touch FilenameUtils, while the targeted FilenameUtils/FileSystemUtils suite is 66/66 green. The one real shortfall is mechanism: a {".", ".."} blocklist instead of upstream's RFC3986/IPv4/IPv6 host-name allowlist, which makes it a strict subset — it passes 12/14 official assertions, failing only the non-traversal "\\-server\..." malformed-hostname hardening cases.
